messages.content: Retrieve Personal Info and Job History data of a specific employee whose ID is 345 in company 'ABC Ltd.'

function.name: employee_fetch_data
function.description: Fetches the detailed data for a specific employee in a given company. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

employee_id.description: The unique ID of the employee.

data_field.description: Fields of data to be fetched for the employee (Optional). Default is ['Personal Info']

message.reasoning:
The user wants to retrieve Personal Info and Job History data for employee ID 345 in company ABC Ltd. The function employee_fetch_data accepts company_name, employee_id, and data_field. The data_field can be "Personal Info" | "Job History" | "Payroll" | "Attendance"[].

We need to pass data_field as an array of strings? The type says data_field?: "Personal Info" | "Job History" | "Payroll" | "Attendance"[], but that seems ambiguous. It might mean data_field can be one of those strings or an array of "Attendance"? Actually the type is weird: data_field?: "Personal Info" | "Job History" | "Payroll" | "Attendance"[], meaning data_field can be either a string "Personal Info", "Job History", "Payroll", or an array of "Attendance"? That doesn't make sense. Possibly they meant data_field?: ("Personal Info" | "Job History" | "Payroll" | "Attendance")[]? But the type says "Attendance"[] which is an array of "Attendance"? That seems like a mistake. But we can guess that data_field should be an array of strings specifying which fields to fetch. The user wants Personal Info and Job History. So we should pass data_field: ["Personal Info", "Job History"].

Thus we call the function with company_name: "ABC Ltd.", employee_id: 345, data_field: ["Personal Info", "Job History"].
